mali-office-du-niger-hamlets.whole: By the World Bank's own completion report, the project developed 6,209 hectares of irrigated land against a revised target of 6,400, including the 2,700 hectares planned at Office du Niger, about 2,200 of them at Sabalibougou. It counted 247,720 direct beneficiaries against a target of 300,000, and rice yields on the large Office du Niger perimeters of 7.19 tonnes a hectare against a target of 6.35. The Bank disbursed US$71.72 million and rated the overall outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, putting the economic return at completion at 11.7% against 34% expected at appraisal, and net present value at US$13.9 million against US$184.2 million, which it says shows the appraisal figures were over-optimistic. These figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

zambia-camdex-copper-revenue.whole: The claim collected nothing through the English courts: the garnishee order was never made final, and the later New York case ended in an out-of-court settlement on undisclosed terms, so what Camdex received is not public (ECB working paper). On Zambia's side of the ledger, a policy framework paper of 10 March 1999, prepared by the Zambian authorities with IMF and World Bank staff, gives copper production of 314,000 tonnes in both 1996 and 1997, copper exports of 327,000 and 301,000 tonnes at US$1,734 and US$2,156 a tonne, real growth of 6.6% then 3.3%, and average inflation of 43.1% then 24.4%. The same paper puts debt service before rescheduling at 40.7% of exports in 1996 and 28.8% in 1997, the net present value of external public debt at about 510% of exports at end-1998, and arrears to non-Paris Club bilateral creditors at about US$300 million; Zambia planned to seek relief under the HIPC Initiative. That paper does not mention commercial creditors or any litigation. The figures come from the government and the two lenders; no independent check was found.

penarroya-cobrac-santo-amaro-lead.whole: No figures for the smelter's lead output, revenue or taxes were found. It made lead ingots from ore mined at Boquira in the Bahian semi-arid interior, from 1960 until it was abandoned in December 1993 (Geousp; Ambiente & Sociedade). In 1974 Cobrac asked to raise its metallic lead capacity from 30,000 to 45,000 tonnes a year; Bahia's government refused and suggested moving the plant to the Aratu industrial centre, according to a 2024 research project at the Universidade da Integracao Internacional da Lusofonia Afro-Brasileira citing a 2003 UNDP report. Sources differ on the workforce: the same 2024 project says about 2,500 people worked there but gives no source for it, while the only headcount in the peer-reviewed literature is a 1983 occupational study of 216 Cobrac employees (Ambiente & Sociedade, 2013).
penarroya-cobrac-santo-amaro-lead.searched: Ambiente & Sociedade review of 40 years of Santo Amaro research (Andrade and Moraes, 2013), the Geousp article already cited in the case, and a 2024 Unilab research project; searched in Portuguese for Cobrac/Plumbum production tonnage, employment and tax figures and found none.

multan-wwtp-suraj-miani-crops.whole: The loans were meant to serve 21 towns and 3.6 million people in low-income communities. ADB approved US$90 million and disbursed US$49.8 million, and records 166 of 172 subprojects completed, including 71 of 80 sewerage and wastewater subprojects, those finished after the loans closed in December 2009 being paid for out of government funds; community development and land development for the poor were not done, and some downstream treatment plants and landfills were still incomplete. ADB's two offices disagree on the result: the project team's completion report rated the project Successful and highly efficient, its evaluation department rated it Less than Successful and less than relevant, and neither says whether the Multan plant was finished. The evaluation department also reports urban poverty in Punjab rising from 13.1% to 16.8% between 2005 and 2009 against a target of cutting it to 22%, diarrhoea in children under five falling from 20.3% to 14.3%, and water- and hygiene-related hospital cases down 15%. All of these figures are the lender's own; no independent check was found.

shell-vila-carioca-contamination.whole: No figures for the terminal's storage capacity, the volumes it handled, its workforce or its taxes were found. Minutes of a 2005 meeting of Sao Paulo's municipal environment council record that Shell came to the Ipiranga district in 1940 to store and distribute petroleum products, and that from 1953 the site also produced agrochemicals. A 2005 report in Sesc Sao Paulo's magazine quotes a Shell press adviser, Luciano Frucht, saying remediation work at the base was continuing, and records a December 2004 agreement between Shell and the labour prosecution service on health measures for workers and former employees, with no compensation offered to residents at that date. No cost was published for the remediation.
shell-vila-carioca-contamination.searched: Sao Paulo municipal environment council (CADES) minutes, the Sesc Sao Paulo report already cited in the case, and searches in Portuguese for the terminal's capacity, throughput, employment and remediation cost; nothing found.

equatorial-palm-oil-jogbahn.whole: By the company's own reporting to the London market, about 7,900 hectares had been planted in Liberia since 2011, 6,470 of them at the Palm Bay estate in Grand Bassa, of which 5,156 hectares were mature enough to harvest by June 2019; 1,418 hectares were planted at Butaw, out of an 8,011-hectare concession there. A mill at Palm Bay, rated at 30 tonnes an hour, was commissioned in the third quarter of 2018, and fresh fruit bunch harvests rose from about 2,000 to more than 4,000 tonnes a month over the three months to June 2019, with the oil extraction rate up from 22% to 25%. For the six months to 31 March 2019 the company reported group revenue of US$85,000 and a loss of US$4.73 million, and its Liberian joint venture revenue of US$1.16 million. In June 2019 it cut about 155 jobs at Butaw, roughly 70% of that estate's workforce. These are company figures; no independent check was found.

heinda-tin-mine-myaung-pyo.whole: No production, revenue, royalty or employment figures for the mine were found. Myanmar's EITI reconciliation report for 2015-16 does not name Pongpipat or Heinda, and reports tin only for the state enterprise sector as a whole. A 2019 Chulalongkorn University thesis puts the concession at 8.23 square kilometres (2,058 acres), with an active mining zone of 1.24 square kilometres; the tonnages it gives are ore reserve and resource estimates, not output. In a statement published in The Nation in September 2017 as part of a settlement, Myanmar Pongpipat said it had provided free water and electricity to more than 400 families near the mine, sent a mobile medical team every month, and had water analysed by Kasetsart University in Thailand, which it said showed no contamination; it gave no production, investment, wage or spending figures, and no independent check of these claims was found.

shell-ogbodo-isiokpo-spill.whole: Shell's Nigerian joint venture produced 899,000 barrels of oil a day in 1997 from more than 80 fields, a figure from SPDC's own 1998 environmental document as quoted by Human Rights Watch; the US Energy Information Administration put that at more than 40% of Nigeria's output, against national production of 2.21 million barrels a day over the first nine months of 1997. The venture was owned 55% by the state company NNPC, 30% by Shell, 10% by Elf and 5% by Agip. Under a memorandum negotiated in 1991, at crude prices between US$12.50 and US$23 a barrel the venture kept US$3 a barrel for shareholders and future investment and US$2 for notional operating costs, and the remainder went to the government (SPDC's own brief, quoted by Human Rights Watch). No figures were found for what the Ogbodo field itself produced, or for what Shell spent on the clean-up beyond the settlement already recorded.
shell-ogbodo-isiokpo-spill.searched: Human Rights Watch's 1999 Nigeria report chapter on the oil companies (quoting SPDC's own documents and US EIA); Shell Nigeria's history page returned no figures, and no field-level output figure for Ogbodo was found.

tayan-nuur-altain-khuder.whole: In a March 2014 presentation to investors, the parent company gave the mine's capacity as 2.3 million tonnes a year, production of 2.2 million tonnes in 2013 and a target of 3.5 million for 2014, and said it held 33% of Mongolian iron ore production; iron ore made up 33% of Mongolia's exports, and the country's iron ore exports came to US$700 million in 2013 (SOMO, Impacts of the global iron ore sector, citing the company presentation and the Mongolian Mining Journal). The governor of Tseel soum told SOMO in August 2014 that the mine was running at about 30% of capacity. SOMO reports no revenue, tax or employment figures, and says neither Altain Khuder nor its parent has published annual reports or accounts; Moody's put production cost at US$45 a tonne in 2011, a figure the company called outdated without giving a newer one. EBRD board minutes of 31 January 2012 record the US$30 million loan and US$25 million of equity, and the company put the bank's stake at 5%. The output figures are the company's own; no independent check was found.
tayan-nuur-altain-khuder.searched: SOMO's 2014 sector report Impacts of the global iron ore sector, which collects the company's own production figures, the EBRD board minutes and interviews with the Tseel soum governor; no company accounts were found.

bnp-rwanda-1994-arms-transfer.whole: What the money is alleged to have bought was one arms consignment. The Mail & Guardian, reporting excerpts of the UN international commission of inquiry's third report of 28 October 1996, wrote that Willem 'Ters' Ehlers admitted to the commission that he was involved in a June 1994 consignment of 80 tonnes of rifles, grenades and ammunition sent from the Seychelles to Goma, then in Zaire, on the Rwandan border, worth well over one million rand. Ehlers told the commission he believed the cargo was for the Zairean armed forces. The report itself was not public at the time, and Human Rights Watch's arms project, whose earlier work prompted the inquiry, called for its release. No figure was found for what the bank earned on the transfers, and the French investigation has produced no charge or ruling.

yakjin-veng-sreng-2014.whole: The Phnom Penh Post reported in 2014 that close to 3,000 people worked at Yakjin's factories in Cambodia, with Gap and Wal-Mart among its customers. The Worker Rights Consortium describes the firm as the third-largest Korean-owned garment factory owner in the country, and records the US investment firm Carlyle Group taking a majority stake in December 2013. After the strike, Yakjin sent a labour-rights consultant, Gare Smith, to Phnom Penh for a week in mid-August 2014; the company said his preliminary assessment found 'significant areas of strength as well as some areas for improvement', and no final report was published. No figures were found for the factory's output, exports, wages or taxes.

vedan-thi-vai-river.whole: Vedan's Vietnamese arm was set up on 1 August 1991 with US$183 million of capital and, by its own account in 2013, had put more than US$500 million into Vietnam and employed over 3,000 people, making monosodium glutamate, starch and modified starches, lysine, caustic soda and animal feed (VCCI News). It reported revenue in Vietnam of US$166 million in 2024, down 4% on the year, which was 43.7% of the group's US$380.2 million and its largest market, and 3,830 staff at the end of 2024; the Vietnamese subsidiary is taxed on profits at 15% rather than the standard 20% (The Investor, from the group's reporting). These are company figures; no independent check was found.

drc-war-economy-bank-channels.whole: The Panel of Experts put what this trade delivered to those running it in figures. It estimated the Rwandan Patriotic Army could earn about US$20 million a month from coltan, buying at about US$10 a kilo from small dealers against about US$200 a kilo at export, and at least US$250 million over 18 months after the highest estimated costs, with Rwanda Metals exporting at least 100 tonnes a month. It says a 'Congo desk' took 5% of the value from diamond dealers before each transaction, about US$200,000 a month from a trading house with US$4 million of monthly turnover, about US$2 million a year each from two dealers, and roughly US$4 million over two years for granting operating authorisations. Rwanda's official defence budget was about US$70 million, some 3% of GDP and 29% of the national budget, against the Panel's own estimate of US$51.6 million a year for aircraft transport and pay for 25,000 troops in the Congo (paragraphs 110 to 113); the Panel agreed with President Kagame that this was a self-financing war. Of the US$1 million BCDI lent SONEX in mid-1999, US$200,000 to US$300,000 had been repaid by February 2000 and about US$700,000 in all according to sources the Panel calls reliable. Rwanda rejected the report: its government spokesman Joseph Bideri called the charges 'without foundation' and said it named people and companies that do not exist, and Uganda and Burundi denied them too (Mail & Guardian, April 2001).
drc-war-economy-bank-channels.searched: The full text of the UN Panel of Experts report S/2001/357 (GlobalSecurity mirror), read in two parts for the Congo desk and coltan estimates, and the Mail & Guardian report of the governments' denials.

arab-bank-hamas-transfers-verdict.whole: Arab Bank was founded in Jerusalem in 1930 and moved to Amman in 1948. For 2014, the year of the verdict, it reported net profit of US$577 million, up 15%, a balance sheet of US$45.6 billion and deposits of US$35 billion, with operations in 30 countries (the bank's own results, reported by Reuters via Gulf News). The Jordan Times, writing during the trial, described it as the preferred bank of the international development and donor community in the Palestinian territories, processing payments for US and European governments, the United Nations and major charities, holding the Palestinian Authority account into which Israel pays the tax and customs revenue it collects on the Authority's behalf, and employing nearly 1,000 people in 27 branches there. The bank said it had provided routine banking services in line with counter-terrorism laws and had no intention of supporting Hamas. The 2015 settlement is confidential, so the sums paid are not public.
arab-bank-hamas-transfers-verdict.searched: Reuters report of Arab Bank's 2014 results via Gulf News, and the Jordan Times profile of the bank published during the New York trial; the settlement amount is confidential and no figure was found.
